EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
Minnesota Dealer Sells 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X Coupe 3LZ ZTK for $107,000 Over MSRP
22 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
There's a very interesting story behind this particular ZR1X, and there's nothing collectors love more than buying a car with an interesting story behind it. Actually, I think everyone would enjoy that. It's the equivalent of George Costanza buying an '89 LeBaron just because he thought it was once owned by Jon Voight.
By the way, George was duped in more ways than one regarding that car, and so were we. It was presented on the show as an '89 LeBaron, when in reality it was a 1984 Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country Convertible according to the IMCDB. His car belonged to the earlier K-car based LeBaron generation. So yeah, Georgie boy was deceived.
Where am I going with this? Well, like I said, there's an interesting story behind this 2026 ZR1X as well. The car was used by General Motors as a pre-production evaluation vehicle, also known as a Captured Test Fleet (CTF) vehicle - part of their internal testing and evaluation program. To clarify, this wasn't some experimental/engineering prototype or even a regular pre-production vehicle.
The latter would often come with provisional components in order to mirror a final spec. A "close but no cigar" type of thing. Whereas a CTF vehicle is basically a near-production car driven by GM personnel to identify any issues before customer deliveries can commence. This Vette was "tested" for only 302 miles before ending up with a Minneapolis-based dealer, who then decided to auction it off to the highest bidder.
According to the sticker, this would have retailed for $247,855, and the price for which it just sold is an impressive $355,000 (plus a buyer's fee). While that might sound like a lot (and it is), I believe this is now one of the cheapest ZR1X models sold at auction in recent months. The absolute cheapest one was a Red Mist Metallic example with 1,200 miles on the clock that exchanged hands for $315,000 last month.
In terms of specs, this car is finished in black and comes with a carbon-fiber rear wing, hood spoiler, and dive planes - all courtesy of the Carbon Fiber Aero Package. Additionally, it also features a carbon fiber rear split window, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, plus a set of Carbon Flash 20" and 21" forged wheels rocking Michelin tires and carbon-ceramic discs.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Sky Cool Gray leather GT2 bucket seats, carbon fiber trim accents, a performance data and video recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a 14-speaker Bose Performance Series sound system, a head-up display, and loads more. This thing is loaded.
As for the engine, you already know what you're rocking with. It's a twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack. Together, they combine for 1,250 horsepower and 973 lb-ft of torque, sending everything to all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic.
